## Purpose and Entry Point
This is a GitHub-maintained, Markdown-native catalog of project-based programming tutorials. The primary artifact and user entry point is `README.md`, organized by programming language and topical subcategories; it links outward rather than hosting applications or tutorial code.

## Content Model
`README.md` is both the content store and presentation layer. Its table of contents anchors language sections, which contain curated Markdown links, optional descriptions, and ordered multipart tutorial groupings. The repository has no database, API, build artifact, or deployed application.

## Contribution Boundary
Contributors modify the catalog through GitHub issues and pull requests. Contribution expectations and content-format rules are defined in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; standardized intake is provided by `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/1-broken-link.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/2-tutorial-suggestion.yml`, and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. This separates unstructured external suggestions from reviewed changes to the canonical README.

## README Validation
A Python validation entry point, `scripts/check_readme.py`, checks README structure/content as part of repository governance. It is the principal local automation component, with duplicate-link exceptions recorded in `scripts/lint-allow-duplicates.txt`. The flow is: README edit → validation script → PR acceptance or correction.

## External-Link Integrity Pipeline
The catalog’s main operational dependency is the availability of third-party tutorial URLs. Link checking is managed by `.github/workflows/link-rot.yml`; domain-specific behavior or exclusions are represented in `scripts/linkcheck-domains.txt`, and persistent link-rot tracking is stored in `.github/link-rot-state.json`. This establishes a periodic automated feedback loop from remote HTTP resources into repository maintenance.

## GitHub Automation and Lifecycle
GitHub Actions provides the runtime/infrastructure; there is no application runtime beyond Python for repository scripts and GitHub-hosted workflow execution. `.github/workflows/validate-pr.yml` gates proposed changes, `.github/workflows/link-rot.yml` monitors external references, and `.github/workflows/stale-prs.yml` manages unattended review work. GitHub/Gitter are the material external services for collaboration and community contact.

## Control Flow
The dominant control flow is editorial: a contributor proposes a tutorial or broken-link fix → PR validation checks repository conventions → maintainers review and merge → `README.md` becomes the published catalog on GitHub. Separately, scheduled link-rot automation detects unhealthy outbound links, creating maintenance work that feeds back through the same issue/PR process.
